mainTopic: שמואל's view on unintended acts, mixing hot and cold water on שבת, and a new משנה on adding spices to a boiling pot
overview: This amud opens with the last word of שמואל's ruling: pouring water into a hot urn is permitted even if it hardens the metal. The גמרא asks whether שמואל holds like רבי שמעון. It challenges this from שמואל's own ruling that one may put out a hot metal coal in a public area, but not a wood coal. The answer is that שמואל follows רבי שמעון on דבר שאין מתכוין, but follows רבי יהודה on מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. רבינא learns from this that a dangerous thorn may be moved in a public area in steps of less than four אמות. In a כרמלית, it may be moved even farther. The גמרא then quotes a ברייתא in which בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about pouring hot water into cold and cold into hot. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא forbids, and רב נחמן rules like him. A discussion about a basin shows that he cannot be forbidding hot into cold, since then there could be no hot washing on שבת at all. So he forbids only cold into hot, and he holds that the two schools never disagreed about this. רבא was lenient about pouring either way into a basin, based on a ברייתא of רבי חייא that says 'pour'. Finally, a new משנה rules that spices may not be added to a boiling pot even after it is taken off the fire.

steps.title: End of שמואל's ruling: it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: This is the final word of שמואל's ruling. One may add water to a hot urn even in an amount that hardens the metal, because the person does not intend that result.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Even if the water is enough to harden the metal of the urn, it] is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word closes שמואל's ruling from the end of the previous section. Pouring water into a hot metal urn is allowed even if it hardens the metal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hardening metal (צירוף) is normally a forbidden מלאכה. שמואל still permits it here, because the person only wants to heat or add water, not to harden the urn. That ruling is what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: Hardening or tempering metal by cooling it while hot (the background case here)

phrases.notes: Completes שמואל's statement: even enough to harden the urn is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuation of שמואל's ruling that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adding water to a hot urn is permitted even if it unintentionally hardens the metal.

steps.title: Does שמואל hold like רבי שמעון? A contradiction from the hot coal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שמואל follows רבי שמעון. It then challenges this with another ruling of שמואל: one may put out a metal coal in a public area, but not a wood coal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we saying that שמואל holds like רבי שמעון? But שמואל himself said: one may extinguish a hot metal coal in a public area so that people will not be hurt, but not a wood coal. If you think he holds like רבי שמעון, then even a wood coal should be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that permitting the urn sounds like רבי שמעון's view. It then attacks that idea using a different ruling of שמואל that seems stricter than רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting out a metal coal is only forbidden מדרבנן, so the רבנן allowed it to protect the public. Putting out a wood coal is forbidden מדאורייתא, and שמואל forbids it. But the person only wants to prevent injury, so רבי שמעון would treat it as exempt. That means שמואל should have allowed the wood coal too.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces a suggested conclusion that will be tested)
A glowing piece of hot metal
And if it would enter your mind (if you assume...)

steps.confusionAlert: The metal coal is not 'not fire' in the sense of having no law at all. Putting it out is still a forbidden act, but only מדרבנן. That is why public safety can override it, while the wood coal (forbidden מדאורייתא) stays forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵימְרָא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: Is that to say that Shmuel holds like Rabbi Shimon?
One may extinguish a coal of metal
so that the public will not be injured by it,
but not a coal of wood.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן —
phrases.english: And if you think he holds like Rabbi Shimon —
even of wood should also [be permitted]!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from שמואל's urn ruling and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that שמואל holds like רבי שמעון in general.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון exempts מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, yet שמואל forbids putting out a wood coal, which is exactly that kind of act. So שמואל cannot fully agree with רבי שמעון.

steps.title: שמואל splits: רבי שמעון on unintended acts, רבי יהודה on labor not needed for itself
steps.stepSummary: שמואל follows רבי שמעון on דבר שאין מתכוין. On מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, he follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On an unintended act, he holds like רבי שמעון. On a מלאכה done not for its own purpose, he holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון has two separate leniencies, and שמואל accepts only one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The urn case is a דבר שאין מתכוין: the hardening simply happens without the person meaning to do it. There שמואל agrees with רבי שמעון and permits. The wood coal case is a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה: the person does mean to extinguish, just not for the usual purpose. There שמואל agrees with רבי יהודה that it is forbidden מדאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: An unintended act: a forbidden result happens without the person meaning to do it
A labor done deliberately, but not for the purpose the מלאכה is normally done for
תנא who holds one is liable even for מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה

steps.whatToRemember: Two different concepts: דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted for שמואל (like רבי שמעון). מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה is forbidden מדאורייתא for שמואל (like רבי יהודה).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two concepts. In דבר שאין מתכוין you do not intend the act at all. In מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה you fully intend the act, just not for its usual goal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This split explains how one אמורא can follow different תנאים on different principles. It also sets up רבינא's practical ruling in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: In an unintended act, he holds like Rabbi Shimon;

phrases.aramaic: בִּמְלָאכָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה לְגוּפָהּ סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: in a labor not needed for its own sake, he holds like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two separate principles of רבי שמעון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל either fully follows רבי שמעון or does not follow him at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי שמעון only on דבר שאין מתכוין, and follows רבי יהודה on מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.

steps.title: רבינא: moving a dangerous thorn in public areas
steps.stepSummary: רבינא draws a practical rule from שמואל: the רבנן did not make their decrees apply where the public is in danger. So a thorn in the public domain may be moved in steps of less than four אמות, and in a כרמלית even farther.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Therefore, a thorn in the public domain may be carried in steps of less than four אמות at a time. In a כרמלית, it may be carried even a long distance.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא applies שמואל's principle to a new case: a thorn lying where people could step on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying four אמות in רשות הרבים is forbidden מדאורייתא, so it stays forbidden. Carrying less than four אמות is only forbidden מדרבנן, and public safety overrides it. In a כרמלית, all carrying is forbidden only מדרבנן, so any distance is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: In repeated steps, each less than four אמות
An in-between area that is neither public nor private, where carrying is forbidden only מדרבנן

steps.whatToRemember: Where the public is in danger, the רבנן did not apply their decrees. But a איסור דאורייתא stays in place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a practical guide for removing hazards on שבת.

phrases.english: Therefore, a thorn in the public domain —
one carries it in steps of less than four cubits each;
and in a karmelit, even a lot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle behind שמואל's metal-coal ruling to a new practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dangerous thorn may be moved less than four אמות at a time in רשות הרבים, and any distance in a כרמלית.

steps.title: New משנה line: בית שמאי and בית הלל on mixing hot and cold water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה and brings a ברייתא. בית שמאי allow only hot into cold. בית הלל allow both directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה says:] 'But one may put...' The רבנן taught: A person may put hot water into cold water, but not cold into hot. These are the words of בית שמאי. בית הלל say: Both hot into cold and cold into hot are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and introduces a ברייתא that discusses mixing hot and cold water on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי worry that cold water poured into hot water gets cooked, since the hot water underneath is stronger. Hot poured into cold gets cooled, so it is fine. בית הלל permit both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (marks a quote from the משנה being discussed)
The two classic schools of the תנאים

phrases.english: A person may place hot water into cold,
and cold into hot are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: only hot into cold. בית הלל: both directions are permitted.

steps.title: Limiting בית הלל: a cup versus a bath
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits בית הלל's leniency to a cup. In a bath, only hot into cold is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? With a cup. But with a bath: hot into cold is allowed, but not cold into hot.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא narrows בית הלל's ruling so it does not apply to every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cup holds only a little water, so the cold water does not really get cooked. A bath holds a large amount of hot water, which can actually cook cold water poured into it. In that case בית הלל agree to the stricter rule.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (introduces a limitation)

phrases.english: When are these words said? With a cup;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of בית הלל's leniency from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל permit both directions only in a cup. In a bath, only hot into cold is permitted.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא forbids
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא disagrees and forbids. At first glance this seems to mean he forbids even hot into cold in a bath. Step 12 corrects this reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן מנסיא forbids.
steps.whatsHappening: A dissenting תנא gives a stricter view on the bath case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a first reading, he responds to the bath clause and forbids even hot water poured into cold. This is stricter than the view the ברייתא gave for בית הלל. Step 12 will show that he is really responding to the first clause and forbids only cold into hot.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who takes the strict position here

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya forbids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting, stricter view on the bath case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Initial reading: in a bath, even hot into cold is forbidden. Step 12 revises this to: he forbids cold into hot only.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like רבי שמעון בן מנסיא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן decides the הלכה follows the strict view of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives the final ruling on the ברייתא's disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן rules like the dissenting view of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. At this point it sounds like even hot into cold in a bath is forbidden. Steps 11-12 show that this reading leads to an impossible result, and they correct it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who decides the הלכה here

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן rules like רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. At this point we read him as forbidding even hot into cold in a bath. Steps 11-12 show that reading cannot stand: he actually forbids only cold into hot.

phrases.english: The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute in favor of the dissent in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. The scope of his ruling is reinterpreted in step 12: he forbids only cold into hot.

steps.title: רב יוסף thinks a basin is like a bath
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף assumes that a basin (סֵפֶל) has the same law as a bath (אמבטי).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף wanted to say: a basin is like a bath.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף suggests that a washing basin follows the same rules as a bath. This means pouring water into it would be restricted the way it is in a bath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 6 set different rules for a cup and for a bath. A basin falls somewhere in between, so רב יוסף places it in the stricter bath category. This sets up the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A basin or tub used for washing
He thought to say (an early assumption, not a final view)

phrases.english: a basin is like a bath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the cup and bath distinction to a basin
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A basin has the status of a bath (initial assumption)

steps.title: אביי cites רבי חייא: a basin is not like a bath
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's view by quoting a ברייתא of רבי חייא saying a basin is not like a bath.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: רבי חייא taught that a basin is not like a bath.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף. He quotes a teaching that says a basin is not like a bath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's assumption runs straight into a ברייתא. A ברייתא outranks an אמורא's guess, so the basin is not treated with the strictness of a bath.

phrases.english: A basin is not like a bath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי, תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יוסף's assumption that a basin equals a bath
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts the ברייתא of רבי חייא

steps.title: Then there would be no hot washing on שבת at all
steps.stepSummary: Under the first assumption, plus רב נחמן's ruling for רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, washing with hot water on שבת would be impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, according to the original assumption that a basin is like a bath, and רב נחמן ruled like רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, there would be no washing with hot water on שבת at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב יוסף's idea leads to an unacceptable result. Nobody could wash with hot water on שבת in any way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא forbids even hot into cold in a bath. If a basin counts as a bath, then every way of mixing water for washing is forbidden. That result is impossible, so this reading of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא and רב נחמן must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: According to what we first thought

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not only against רב יוסף, who was already rejected. It mainly shows that our understanding of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's view (steps 7-8) cannot be right.

phrases.english: And according to what entered the mind at first
that a basin is like a bath,
the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya,
then on Shabbat there is no washing with hot water at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines step 9 with steps 7-8 to reach an impossible result
steps.kashyaTarget: The understanding of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's view together with רב נחמן's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio: every method of warm washing would be forbidden, which cannot be

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא refers to the first clause
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא is not speaking about the bath. He is speaking about the earlier case, and he forbids only cold into hot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think רבי שמעון is talking about the last clause? He is talking about the first clause: בית הלל permit both hot into cold and cold into hot, and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא forbids cold into hot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing which part of the ברייתא רבי שמעון בן מנסיא was responding to. His point is about the general case, not the bath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His disagreement is with בית הלל's leniency in the first clause. He forbids only cold into hot and still allows hot into cold. So רב נחמן's ruling does not ban warm washing, because hot into cold stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think...? (introduces a corrected reading)

phrases.aramaic: מִי סָבְרַתְּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַסֵּיפָא קָאֵי?
phrases.english: Do you think Rabbi Shimon refers to the latter clause?
He refers to the first clause:

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַסֵּיפָא קָאֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-attaching the statement to a different clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא forbade even hot into cold in a bath
steps.terutzMaskana: He forbids only cold into hot, in the general case

steps.title: Does this make him follow בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: If he forbids cold into hot, he seems to side with בית שמאי against בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבי שמעון בן מנסיא holds like בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The new reading raises a problem. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא now sounds exactly like בית שמאי, and we normally follow בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי allowed only hot into cold, as in step 5. That is the same rule now given to רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. If so, how could רב נחמן rule like him and go against בית הלל?

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (proposes a troubling conclusion)

phrases.english: Shall we say Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya
stated his view like Beit Shammai?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא דְּאָמַר כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 12 combined with רב נחמן's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה should not follow בית שמאי against בית הלל

steps.title: In his tradition בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא holds that בית שמאי and בית הלל agreed on this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי שמעון בן מנסיא had a different tradition. In his version, both schools agree that only hot into cold is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not siding with בית שמאי against בית הלל. He is reporting that there was no dispute at all. So ruling like him does not go against בית הלל.
steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: a basin is not like a bath. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא forbids cold into hot, and רב נחמן follows him. He holds that בית שמאי and בית הלל both agree on this, so hot into cold remains allowed.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בְּדָבָר זֶה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He follows בית שמאי against בית הלל
steps.terutzMaskana: He holds there was no dispute between the schools on this point

steps.title: רבא was not strict about a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע reports seeing רבא act leniently with a vessel, without separating hot and cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: I saw that רבא was not strict about a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: A new report begins. רבא allowed mixing hot and cold in a vessel either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of the strict view just explained. רבא did not insist on hot into cold only when using a basin. The next step gives his source.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
that he was not strict about a vessel

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזֵינָא לֵיהּ לְרָבָא דְּלָא קָפֵיד אַמָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a lenient practice about vessels
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a vessel, both hot into cold and cold into hot are allowed

steps.title: רבא's source: רבי חייא's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא based his leniency on רבי חייא's ברייתא allowing a jug of water to be put into a basin either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was based on what רבי חייא taught: A person may put a jug of water into a basin of water, both hot into cold and cold into hot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רבא's leniency comes from. It is a ברייתא that allows both directions with a jug and a basin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explicitly allows cold into hot in a basin. That supports רבא's lenient practice. It also fits אביי's statement that a basin is not like a bath.

phrases.english: A person may place a jug of water

steps.title: Maybe the jug acts as a barrier
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא challenges the proof: the jug may separate the two waters, so it is not real mixing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to רב אשי: Perhaps it is different there, because the vessel separates them!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא questions the proof. Maybe the ברייתא means placing a whole jug into the basin, with its walls keeping the waters apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the jug's walls separate the hot from the cold, the waters never really mix. Then the ברייתא says nothing about pouring, and רבא's leniency loses its source.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said to Rav Ashi:

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using the ברייתא as proof for pouring
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The jug may be a barrier, so there is no direct mixing

steps.title: The ברייתא actually says pour
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the correct wording of the ברייתא is 'pour', so the waters truly mix.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Pour' was stated. A person may pour a jug of water into a basin of water, both hot into cold and cold into hot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends the proof by correcting the wording of the ברייתא. It is about pouring the water out, not placing the jug inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the word 'pour', there is no barrier, because the water itself goes into the basin. So the ברייתא really does permit cold into hot in a basin, and רבא's leniency stands.
steps.whatToRemember: In a basin (not a bath), the ברייתא of רבי חייא lets you pour water either way, hot into cold or cold into hot.

phrases.english: A person may pour a jug of water

steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא spoke of placing a jug, so its walls separate the waters
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא says 'pour', so the waters truly mix and the leniency holds

steps.title: New משנה: no spices into a boiling pot taken off the fire
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that spices may not be put into a pot that was taken off the fire while still boiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A stew pot or a pot that was taken off the fire while boiling: one may not put spices into it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that even off the fire, a boiling pot can still cook spices, so you may not add them on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pot is a כלי ראשון, the first vessel that sat on the fire. It is hot enough to cook even after being removed. So adding spices counts as cooking on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the source for the idea that a כלי ראשון can cook even off the fire, a key concept in the laws of cooking on שבת.

phrases.english: The stew pot and the pot
that one removed (from the fire) while boiling
one may not put spices into them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה about cooking in a vessel off the fire
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No spices may be added to a boiling pot even after it is removed from the fire
